title: Forever Ephraim
summary: A content-focused portfolio experience designed to showcase writing, marketing, and digital storytelling.
shortDescription: A digital experience built around content, storytelling, and personal publishing.

overview: Forever Ephraim is a content-focused portfolio experience designed to showcase writing, marketing, and digital storytelling.
The experience needed to make content presentation feel clear, personal, and easy to browse.
The site sits closer to a publishing surface than a traditional portfolio, so the structure had to support writing, positioning, and storytelling without overcomplicating the interface.
contribution: Built the frontend with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion.
Structured the experience around content hierarchy, storytelling, and personal publishing.
Implemented responsive layouts that keep writing and marketing content readable across screen sizes.
Focused the interface on clear content presentation without making the experience feel crowded.
challenges: The project needed to support writing, marketing, and digital storytelling without making the experience feel crowded.
The content needed a structure that could stay readable and flexible.
The design had to leave enough room for the writing to carry the experience.
The site also needed responsive layouts that would keep longer text sections comfortable on mobile and desktop.
approach: Focused the build around content hierarchy, clean presentation, and simple navigation.
Built a digital publishing experience where storytelling stays central and the interface supports the message.
Used responsive layouts to keep the work readable across screen sizes.
Applied restrained motion and spacing so the experience could feel personal without becoming visually noisy.
outcome: The result is a digital experience built around content, storytelling, and personal publishing.
The website gives the brand a clearer home for writing and marketing work.
Visitors can move through the experience with less friction because the content is presented with stronger hierarchy and breathing room.
caseStudy.pullQuote: Content-led websites work best when the interface gets out of the way.
